name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,339

clue.text: Informal class run ably on regular basis

indicators.note: a regular basis means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the run of words is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A relaxed class where the running is done well, held now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual dress or manner is relaxed and unofficial, a straightforward synonym of informal.

clue.text: Dish from firm (American) on 8?

blocks.note: CO is short for company
US stands for American
8 down is DOUBLE, so the firm-and-American unit is repeated

explanation.surface: A meal from an American company served on something.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 8 down, which reads DOUBLE: the first four letters are said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African dish of steamed semolina grains, usually served with stew.

clue.text: Unable to move with lengths of thread

blocks.note: first meaning: stuck, left helpless, like a beached boat
second meaning: made of or having strands

explanation.surface: Someone tangled in thread and unable to free themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranded means left stuck without means of leaving, and also composed of twisted fibres or filaments.

clue.text: Drink traps soldier, nimble

indicators.note: a trap catches and holds its prey, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: ale is a beer
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A beer catches out a soldier who is quick on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and nimble both describe moving quickly and lightly, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Poet backing blackleg's case for weapon

indicators.note: backing means standing behind in support, so the poet's piece is placed after the other one

blocks.note: a blackleg is a strike-breaker
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet siding with a strike-breaker, and something about a weapon's case.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British slang for a worker who crosses a picket line, also called a scab.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword or dagger when it is not drawn.

clue.text: Having consuming interests? Abstain: clinic ordered

indicators.note: to order things is to put them into an arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A clinic tells a patient with consuming passions to abstain.
explanation.walkthrough: Consuming interests sounds like absorbing hobbies, but it means literally eating one's own kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats members of its own species, so its interests are literally about consuming them.

clue.text: Special chap probing responsibility for curse

indicators.note: a probe goes inside to investigate, so these pieces sit within the other word

blocks.note: blame is responsibility for a fault
SP is an abbreviation for special
a chap is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A special investigator looking into who is responsible for a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to swear profanely or speak irreverently of God, a form of cursing.

clue.text: Reject seaman over unfinished panel and drug

indicators.note: an unfinished word is missing its final letter, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue, over means placed on top, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
a jury is a panel of people giving a verdict
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sailor turns down an incomplete board and some drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To abjure is to renounce or reject formally, especially a belief or claim.

clue.text: Payment secures posh British understudy

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: the dole is unemployment benefit payment
U means upper-class
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A fee guarantees a part for an upper-class British stand-in actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British name for state unemployment benefit, and U is an old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a stand-in who replaces an actor, much as an understudy replaces a performer.

clue.text: National from this country, artist in Paisley?

blocks.note: for a British newspaper, this country is the United Kingdom
Royal Academician
taken as written
Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish politician and preacher

explanation.surface: Is a citizen of Britain an artist working in paisley fabric patterns?
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley looks like the swirly fabric pattern or the Scottish town, but it is the surname of Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a particular state, and a Ukrainian is a citizen of Ukraine.

clue.text: Rare enigma - endless rite strangely uniting close relations

definitions.note: a gerund phrase describing the noun answer

indicators.note: something endless has lost its end, so the final letter of the word goes
strangely means oddly or out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters of these two words
taken as written before its end goes

explanation.surface: A rare puzzle: an incomplete ritual oddly joins close family.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermarriage can mean marriage between close relatives, so the term describes joining kin in wedlock.

clue.text: Norman journal features historic province

indicators.note: to feature something is to include it, so the answer sits inside the run of letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Norman-era chronicle includes an account of a historic French region.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou was a county and later a province of France, the home of the Angevin kings of England.

clue.text: Vanity of court entertaining in the past is half-forgotten

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other inside it
if half a word is forgotten, only the remaining half of its letters is kept

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
once means formerly
the first half of this two-letter word

explanation.surface: The pride of a royal court that once hosted grand entertainments is now half forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive pride in oneself, the same failing as vanity.

clue.text: Put in danger, empire's lacking answer

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter is taken out of the word before it

blocks.note: imperial means belonging to an empire
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: An empire put at risk because it has no answer to its problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive is the trick: empire's stands for the adjective imperial, which then loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to endanger, a verb phrase meaning exposing someone or something to harm.

clue.text: Unexpectedly urge tax, end up with no cuts?

indicators.note: something unexpected does not follow the expected order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A surprise call for higher taxes ending with no spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuts suggests budget cuts in the surface, but in the definition they are cuts made to a text by a censor.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpurgated text is complete, with no passages removed by an editor or censor.

clue.text: Papers going into gift for head of republic

indicators.note: to go into something is to enter it, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: a present is a gift
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Documents are slipped into a present for a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic has an elected president rather than a monarch as its chief of state.

clue.text: Stimulating quality of quip about city in France subject to guillotine?

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters of the word are turned into a new order
the guillotine cuts off the head, so the first letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
Nancy is a city in Lorraine, France

explanation.surface: A witty quip about a French city during the Revolution's guillotine days.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquancy is the sharp, pleasantly stimulating quality of a flavour or of a remark.

clue.text: At home, looked after fiancée

blocks.note: in means at home
to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: A woman engaged to be married is cared for at home.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one plans to marry, an old-fashioned noun for a betrothed partner.

clue.text: New Senate giving? Taking away, this suggests

indicators.note: a new version of something is remade, so these letters form a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A newly elected Senate is generous, though its taxes take money away.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking away is subtraction, which the minus symbol indicates.
explanation.definitionFit: The minus symbol signals subtraction, so it is the mark that suggests something is being taken away.

clue.text: Popular guardian's responsibility directed to centre

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a ward is a child in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: A well-liked guardian's charge is pointed toward the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Inward describes movement toward the inside or the middle of something.

clue.text: Intensity of Spanish port user on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside of the word is removed and only its ends remain

blocks.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia
first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: The intensity of a holidaymaker's experience in a Spanish port.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is energy and force, so it covers the strength or intensity of an action.

clue.text: Like less pleasant neighbours? More prying, I admitted

indicators.note: someone admitted is let inside, so one letter goes into the other word

blocks.note: nosy means prying, so more prying is nosier
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to being the snoopiest of the unpleasant people next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant neighbours are often loud ones, so noisier describes neighbours who are worse to live beside.

clue.text: Group welcomes extremely upbeat words of appreciation

indicators.note: to welcome a visitor is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: a tribe is a social group
first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A group greets someone with very cheerful words of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is a speech or statement expressing praise, respect or gratitude.

clue.text: Informal business in independent top class holiday island

indicators.note: in places one piece within the outer letters that follow

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
biz is slang for business
A is first class, the top grade

explanation.surface: Casual trade in an independent luxury holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a destination for tourists and clubbers.

clue.text: Like very much portion of salad or eggs

indicators.note: a portion is only part of the whole, so the answer is a stretch of the following letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone loves a helping of salad or of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore something is to love it or be very fond of it, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Got rid of lots once audit prepared

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A firm shed a great deal of stock after its audit was ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Lots looks like a large amount, but here it means lots in a saleroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Items sold at auction are offered as numbered lots, so auctioning them disposes of them.

clue.text: Rodeo hat redesigned for girl

indicators.note: a redesign reshapes the original, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cowboy hat is restyled to fit a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothea is a female first name, and crosswords often define a woman's name simply as a girl.

clue.text: Fellow daddy's excitedly embraced - from Wales?

definitions.note: the name of a man from Wales

indicators.note: excitement throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
something embraced is held within arms, so one letter is wrapped inside the rest

blocks.note: the five letters of this word, with the 's read as is
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: An excited father hugs a man who might be Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, so daddy is excitedly embracing the fellow. Fellow also points at the answer being a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dafydd is the Welsh form of the name David, so its bearer is typically a man from Wales.
